y-m-66-09.s.s2.prompt: Now na ∫ x·ln x dx. Which statement best evaluate choice 'like Hayun, make x be f (part to differentiate)'?
y-m-66-09.s.s2.hint.0: For both choices (f=x or f=ln x), find and write f′ and g, then compare which choice make g easier to find.

y-m-66-09.s.s2.o.a: First you gats find g=∫ ln x dx, so f=ln x look simpler.
y-m-66-09.s.s2.r.a: Dem choose by comparing shape of remaining integral and intermediate calculation wey dem need.
y-m-66-09.s.s2.o.b: x na simplest expression, so e always best to use x as f for any product.
y-m-66-09.s.s2.r.b: Dem generalize one successful case, product with e^x, to all products.
y-m-66-09.s.s2.o.c: You no fit integrate ln x, so e impossible to choose am as g′
y-m-66-09.s.s2.r.c: E think impossible because e no know indefinite integral of ln x dey (x ln x − x).
y-m-66-09.s.s2.explain: If you set f=x and g′=ln x, first you gats find g=x ln x − x. If f=ln x and g′=x, den f′=1/x and g=x²/2, and remaining integral na ∫ (x/2) dx, very simple. So for dis problem better put ln x for part wey dem differentiate.
